cars.variant: Z/28 350 four-speed manual, 3.73 axle — February 1970 US factory reference
cars.specification_market: 1970 US second-generation Camaro Z/28, selected four-speed manual with factory 3.73 axle. Actual Chevrolet February 1970 Power Trains pages 2–6 and AMA 4B supply the reference: 350 cu in nominal, 11.0:1, cast-iron 90-degree OHV V8, four-barrel, 360 gross brake hp at 6000 rpm and 380 gross lb-ft at 4000 rpm. These are advertised gross ratings, not SAE net or wheel output. No inferred cc/kW/Nm conversion, specific Muncie ratio set, optional 4.10 axle, later detuned engine, race preparation or period-test performance figure is selected. The C/D test car was automatic and its published power-peak rpm and torque figures differ; those do not replace the factory reference.
cars.summary: The second-generation Z/28 developed the Camaro’s performance identity with a high-compression 350-cubic-inch V8 and revised steering and road behaviour. Contemporary first-hand testing assessed it as a distinctive road GT while also recording its handling compromises. Count this absent Camaro generation once; engines, RS/SS appearance or performance packages and later years do not add entries.

cars.variant: LS1 Z28 coupe, optional MM6 six-speed manual — 1998 US factory reference
cars.specification_market: 1998 US-market fourth-generation Z28 coupe, optional MM6 six-speed manual, power-team D in the actual factory MVMA table. M30 automatic is standard in this table; the chosen manual is not mislabelled standard. Factory F-car LS1 data: 5665 cc, 10.1:1, 228 kW (305 bhp) at 5200 rpm and 454 Nm (335 lb-ft) at 4000 rpm, SAE J1349 net. Stated metric figures are retained without recalculation. Not the Corvette Y-car 345-hp/350-lb-ft calibration, base L36 V6, SS/1LE package, later-year output or 1970 gross rating. Model year 1998 is not the start of the fourth generation. Factory page 1 identifies Canadian assembly; origin denotes the US Chevrolet programme, not assembly location.
cars.summary: The fourth-generation Camaro carried the affordable V8 pony-car line into its LS-engine era. The selected LS1 Z28 combines the Corvette-derived aluminium-block V8 with a six-speed manual, marking a substantial mechanical evolution within an established American performance family. Count this generation once; LT1/LS1 years, SS packages, transmissions, open-top bodies and anniversaries do not add separate entries.
